# Set up your team, your lab & your Microsoft Learn profile {#sec-lab-01 .unnumbered}

*Exercise 1 · Session 1 lab · Estimated time: 60-90 min*

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
This is the practical task for [Chapter 1: Cloud computing and information security](../chapters/01-cloud-information-security.qmd).
Work through it in your lab group; you talk your answers through at the
session after next (the review runs one session behind). **This page
mirrors the worksheet for reading and reference - the official worksheet
is the PDF distributed via Canvas.**
:::

Three jobs today: (1) form the
**team you will keep for the whole semester and the exam**, (2) build the local Ubuntu laboratory
that is the red thread of this course, and (3) start the Microsoft Learn track that runs alongside it.

::: {.callout-important title="How the labs work (applies all semester)"}
Work through each lab *in your group* and
discuss the answers together. At the next session you briefly talk the teacher through your answers -
*verbally*, just so progress can be tracked (nothing is handed in, signed or graded here). The
review runs *one session behind*, so you always have the week in between: Session 2 $\rightarrow$
Exercise 1; Session 3 $\rightarrow$ Exercise 2; … Session $N$ $\rightarrow$ Exercise $N-1$.
:::

## Form your team (this is also your exam group)

The home exam is done in groups, so the team you form now is the team you will be assessed with.

::: {.callout-note}
Form a group of **3 to 5 people**. Fewer than 3 makes the workload heavy; more than 5 makes
coordination hard. You do *not* register the members here - what matters for the labs is your
group's *progress*, not who is in it. The same group submits the final report, evidence appendix
and screen recording.
:::

- [ ] **Pick a short group name/ID** (e.g. `OSL-07`) and use it on every answer document.

::: {.callout-note}
**The answer documents (read once, apply all term).** Each week you fill in that session's
**answer document** - a Word file (`SKY2100_ExerciseN_Answers.docx`) that mirrors this sheet:
every task, table and question here has a box there. Nothing else is collected. Keep one answer
document per exercise in your group's shared folder. The final home-exam report is built from these
weekly documents, so filling them in properly as you go *is* the exam preparation.
:::

## Build the local laboratory

- [ ] **Confirm virtualisation is enabled.** In your OS task manager (Windows: `Ctrl+Shift+Esc`
  $\rightarrow$ Performance $\rightarrow$ CPU), check that *Virtualization* is **Enabled**;
  otherwise enable Intel VT-x / AMD-V in BIOS/UEFI.
- [ ] **Create and boot an Ubuntu VM** in VMware/VirtualBox ($\geq$2 vCPU, $\geq$4 GB RAM,
  $\geq$25 GB disk). Open a terminal and run `whoami`, `uname -a`, `ip a`.

::: {.callout-warning}
If the VM will not boot, do not get stuck: note it in the answer document, finish Section 3,
and ask an SA. You must not fall behind on the lab thread.
:::

## Cloud transfer: Microsoft Learn

We use the free *Microsoft Learn* "Introduction to Cloud Infrastructure" series as the Azure
side of the course. (Module names verified August 2026.)

- [ ] **Sign in and start Part 1 - "Describe cloud concepts".**

  [learn.microsoft.com/training/paths/microsoft-azure-fundamentals-describe-cloud-concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/paths/microsoft-azure-fundamentals-describe-cloud-concepts/)

  Work through the first units: cloud computing, deployment models, and the shared-responsibility model.
  Note in the answer document which units you completed.

## Azure reflection

Answer in your own words - connect the training to today's lecture.

- [ ] **In the shared-responsibility model, name one thing that is the *provider's* job in SaaS but
  *your* job in IaaS.**
- [ ] **The Microsoft training and the lecture both define "the cloud". Give the *one* difference
  you found most useful between how a vendor (Microsoft) frames it and how the course frames it (from a
  security view).**

::: {.callout-tip title="Aha"}
The two halves of today differed in who was responsible. You build and maintain the local VM
yourself. On Azure you look after only your account and your data, while the provider runs the hardware,
the hypervisor and the platform. That division of labour is the shared-responsibility model, and how
much is your job depends on the service model: IaaS, PaaS or SaaS.
:::

## Knowledge check

Write short answers in the space provided. Tick the correct box for multiple-choice items.

1.  Which is **not** one of the five essential cloud characteristics?
    a) ☐ on-demand self-service
    b) ☐ broad network access
    c) ☐ unlimited free storage
    d) ☐ rapid elasticity

    *Hint: Four are genuine NIST characteristics; one promises something no paid service delivers.*

2.  Name the three CIA properties and give a one-line meaning for each.

    *Hint: One keeps secrets, one prevents undetected tampering, one keeps the service reachable.*

3.  Explain the difference between a **threat**, a **risk** and a **control**, with
    one example of your own.

    *Hint: One is the potential cause, one is likelihood times impact, one is the measure that lowers it.*

4.  Which service model gives the customer the *most* control of the stack?
    a) ☐ SaaS
    b) ☐ PaaS
    c) ☐ IaaS
    d) ☐ SecaaS

    *Hint: The model where you manage the operating system and everything above it.*

5.  Match each to on-prem / IaaS / PaaS / SaaS: "I manage only my data and users" =
    \_\_\_\_\_\_; "I manage the OS upward" = \_\_\_\_\_\_.

    *Hint: The least you manage is 'only data and users'; managing the OS upward is the other extreme.*

6.  In one sentence: why is securing the cloud different from securing an internal server?

    *Hint: The provider now shares the stack with you - think trust boundaries and shared hardware.*

7.  Define **Security as a Service (SecaaS)** and give one example.

    *Hint: Security delivered like any other cloud service: a managed WAF, SIEM or DDoS protection.*

8.  Name the four deployment models and say which one dominates in practice.

    *Hint: Public, private, community - and the blend that dominates in practice.*

9.  The group home exam rewards primarily…
    a) ☐ presentation polish
    b) ☐ consistency between report and evidence
    c) ☐ number of screenshots
    d) ☐ report length

    *Hint: It is not about polish; the report and the evidence have to agree.*

10. True or false: *undisclosed* AI use is the problem, not AI use itself. Briefly justify.

    *Hint: The declaration targets the undisclosed kind; an LLM cannot produce your lab evidence.*

11. Pick one CIA property and name a *later session* where it is the main focus.

    *Hint: Confidentiality → the TLS and access sessions; Integrity → logs and timeline; Availability → load or backup.*

12. (Reflection) Write one question about cloud security you want answered by the end of the course.

---

**Progress check:** Discuss your answers in the group, then
talk the teacher through them verbally at the next session only to track progress; nothing is handed
in, signed or graded.

## Solutions {.unnumbered}

*Work through the lab first, then check here. Model answers are indicative - equivalent reasoning is fine.*

**Note:** Model answers are indicative - accept equivalent reasoning. Multiple-choice
answers are in **bold**.

### Knowledge check

1.  **Unlimited free storage** is not a characteristic. The five are: on-demand self-service,
    broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.
2.  **Confidentiality** - disclosed only to the authorised; **Integrity** - not altered
    without authorisation/detection; **Availability** - reachable when needed.
3.  **Threat** = a potential cause of an unwanted incident; **Risk** = likelihood
    $\times$ impact; **Control** = a measure that reduces the risk. E.g. threat = request
    flood; risk = high for a public service; control = rate limiting / WAF.
4.  **IaaS** gives the customer the most control of the stack.
5.  "Only my data and users" = **SaaS**; "OS upward" = **IaaS**.
6.  Because *control is shared* with the provider: trust boundaries are logical not physical,
    you share infrastructure (multi-tenancy), and depend on an internet-facing control plane.
7.  **SecaaS** = security capabilities consumed as a cloud service; e.g. a managed WAF, cloud
    monitoring/SIEM, or managed DDoS protection.
8.  **Public, Private, Community, Hybrid**; **Hybrid** dominates in practice.
9.  **Consistency between report and evidence.**
10. **True** - the AI declaration penalises *undisclosed* use; an LLM cannot produce your
    lab evidence.
11. Any valid pair, e.g. Confidentiality $\rightarrow$ S6-7; Integrity $\rightarrow$ S9-10;
    Availability $\rightarrow$ S3/S11.
12. Open reflection - no fixed answer.
